claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a child, Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, and other living expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. Alex lives with me and I provide for all their needs - food, clothes, everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just one final question to complete the assessment:

Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any other living arrangement outside your home for an extended period, or are they living with you full-time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now. They're not living with me full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. This is an important detail. I need to understand a bit more about the care arrangement.

How long has Alex been in local authority care - is it more or less than 8 weeks? And does Alex spend any regular time at home with you each week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been more than 8 weeks - about 12 weeks now. As for how much time they spend at home with me... I'm not really sure exactly. Sometimes they come home, but I couldn't tell you exactly how many hours per week. It varies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful to understand your situation.

To clarify the arrangement: does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or does Alex ever spend 2 nights in a row each week at home, or perhaps 7 days or more in a row at home? Even if it varies, knowing the typical pattern would be helpful.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly can't say for certain. Like I said, it really does vary - some weeks might be more, some weeks less. I don't keep track of the exact hours or have a set pattern. I just don't know if it reaches 24 hours or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**Your situation:**
- You meet the basic criteria - you're responsible for Alex (who is 8 years old), you live in the UK, and you provide for their needs
- However, Alex has been in local authority care for about 12 weeks, which is more than the 8-week threshold

**The key issue:**
Normally, after a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks, you're no longer entitled to Child Benefit. However, there's an important exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit if your child spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you.

Since you're unable to confirm whether Alex regularly spends 24 hours or more per week at home, I cannot determine whether you qualify for this exception.

**What you should do:**
I'd recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly. They can:
- Help you work out the exact hours Alex spends at home
- Determine if you qualify for the exception
- Provide specific guidance for your situation

You can contact them by phone or through their online form for changes in circumstances. They'll be able to give you a definitive answer based on a detailed review of Alex's care arrangement.
